tasks.title: Thinking Outside the Box
paras: Does the expression "thinking outside the box" mean what we think it does? This mantra instructs us to consciously dispense with constraints, but what if the box itself prevents us from thinking creatively? "Creativity," as the theorist Edward de Bono notes, "is about bringing into being something that was not there before". He asserts that creative thinking is not a rare biological gift but a skill that enables us to bring new ideas into the world. Our brains obtain information by connecting new input to patterns of previously stored data, so we retain thoughts and ideas that match with what is already in our mental database. By changing our thought processes, we can block these habitual neural networks from getting activated and alter the self-organizing patterns in our heads. Forcing our minds into taking new routes and abandoning our box is what leads to innovative thinking. To achieve this, we can do exercises such as asking what-if questions and changing our angle of observation. Real innovation requires approaching challenges without boxes. Perhaps the best way to eliminate the box is to "set the box on fire." Once you do, you may be amazed by what innovative ideas come to mind.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the first paragraph?

options.A: To suggest readers reconsider a popularly held belief
options.B: To ask readers to avoid overusing an expression
options.C: To raise concerns about outdated instruction methods
options.D: To question the importance of thinking creatively

questions.analysis: 正确答案：A 题型：修辞目的题 原文定位：Does the expression "thinking outside the box" mean what we think it does? …but what if the box itself prevents us from thinking creatively? 正确答案分析：第一段以反问句开头，质疑大家普遍认同的 “跳出盒子思考” 这一说法，引导读者重新思考、反思这个流行观点，而不是盲目接受。 选项分析： (A) To suggest readers reconsider a popularly held belief —— 正确。作者质疑流行说法，让读者重新思考固有观念。 (B) To ask readers to avoid overusing an expression —— 错误。作者不是让读者少用这句话，而是反思这句话背后的理念。 (C) To raise concerns about outdated instruction methods —— 错误。文中未提到 “过时的教学方法”，属于无关信息。 (D) To question the importance of thinking creatively —— 错误。作者全程支持创造性思考，并未质疑其重要性。

questions.stem: The word "mantra" in the passage is closest in meaning to

options.C: a rule that is rarely disobeyed
options.D: a phrase that is repeated often

questions.analysis: 正确答案：D 题型：词汇题 原文定位：This mantra instructs us to consciously dispense with constraints… 正确答案分析：mantra 原指 “咒语、口头禅”，在文中指人们经常重复、广为流传的一句格言（thinking outside the box）。 选项分析： (A) a well-respected teacher 受人尊敬的老师 —— 错误，与人物无关。 (B) a very popular song 流行歌曲 —— 错误，和音乐无关。 (C) a rule that is rarely disobeyed 很少被违反的规则 —— 错误，mantra 不是强制规则，只是常用说法。 (D) a phrase that is repeated often 经常被重复的说法 —— 正确，符合 “口头禅、格言” 的含义。

questions.stem: What does Edward de Bono suggest about creative thinking?

options.A: It is crucial for achieving success in life
options.B: It is a skill that can be developed.
options.C: It is a gift that not all people have.
options.D: It is taught by family members.

questions.analysis: 正确答案：B 题型：细节题 原文定位：He asserts that creative thinking is not a rare biological gift but a skill that enables us to bring new ideas into the world. 正确答案分析：Edward de Bono 明确指出：创造性思维不是天生的天赋，而是一种可以培养的技能。 选项分析： (A) It is crucial for achieving success in life —— 错误。文中未提到 “人生成功”，属于无依据延伸。 (B) It is a skill that can be developed —— 正确。对应 not a gift but a skill。 (C) It is a gift that not all people have —— 错误。与原文完全相反，原文明确说不是天赋。 (D) It is taught by family members —— 错误。文中未提到家人教授创造性思维。

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the passage about neural networks?

options.A: They are responsible for the way we organize information.
options.B: They have the capacity to store a limited amount of data.
options.C: They have a pattern that scientists do not yet understand.
options.D: They are unable to block our negative thought processes.

questions.analysis: 正确答案：A 题型：推理题 原文定位：Our brains obtain information by connecting new input to patterns… we retain thoughts that match our mental database. …block these habitual neural networks… alter the self-organizing patterns in our heads. 正确答案分析：大脑依靠神经网络形成固定模式，组织信息、储存数据、形成思维习惯。因此神经网络负责我们组织信息的方式。 选项分析： (A) They are responsible for the way we organize information. —— 正确。神经网络形成思维模式、组织信息。 (B) They have a capacity to store limited data —— 错误。文中未提储存容量有限。 (C) They have a pattern scientists do not understand —— 错误。文中明确解释了其模式，说明是可理解的。 (D) They are unable to block negative thoughts —— 错误。文中说可以阻断习惯性神经网络，并未提负面思维。

questions.stem: At the end of the passage, what does the author recommend that readers do?

options.A: Ask for help with new challenges
options.B: Get rid of typical ways of thinking
options.C: Avoid tasks that are too difficult

questions.analysis: 正确答案：B 题型：细节题 原文定位：Real innovation requires approaching challenges without boxes. Perhaps the best way to eliminate the box is to "set the box on fire." 正确答案分析：作者建议抛弃、消除盒子（即固有思维模式、常规思路），完全摆脱惯性思考。 选项分析： (A) Ask for help with new challenges —— 错误。文中未提寻求帮助。 (B) Get rid of typical ways of thinking —— 正确。eliminate the box = 摆脱典型、常规的思考方式。 (C) Avoid tasks that are too difficult —— 错误。文中未建议逃避困难任务。 (D) Write down innovative ideas —— 错误。文中未提到要把想法写下来。
